_bidNote: counterStepUsd is a MINIMUM move, not a fixed ladder step. Bids are reciprocal — the buyer moves roughly what the supplier just moved — because a staircase indexed by round number ignores the counterparty entirely and is not how anyone negotiates. maxBidUsd stays a hard ceiling and is framed to the reasoner as a failure condition, not a target: handed a bare ceiling an LLM bids it (measured, 4/4 runs).
_note: The buyer's PRIVATE commercial mandate. Loaded ONLY by the buyer process; it is never published to the directory and never placed in any wire message. `reservationUnitPriceUsd` and `maxTotalCommittedUsd` in particular must never leak — a self-interested seller that learns them extracts every dollar between the buyer's bid and its bound. The no-leak lint test (packages/buyer/src/mandate.test.ts) makes that a failing test, not a code-review hope.
_capNote: maxTotalCommittedUsd is deliberately sized just above ONE settled deal (100u at the autonomous band is at most ~$9,300), so the cross-deal cap actually binds: a single deal fits, a concurrent second one is blocked and escalated. A cap far above the deal value would make the ledger a no-op in the demo.
_budgetNote: maxRounds is a RUNAWAY GUARD, not the stopping rule. A negotiation should end because the supplier stopped moving (minConcessionPerRoundUsd), which is how a negotiator decides; if maxRounds ever fires it means the judgement layer failed, and the buyer logs it as an anomaly. It used to be 6, which made it the de-facto stopping rule and pinned every outcome to arithmetic.
